newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - APN says makes good start to 1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - APN says makes good start to 1997.

text.p: Regional media group Australian Provincial Newspapers Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had made a good start to the current year and a better performance in 1997 was expected.
"1997 has started well. There is certainly a better year in prospect," chief executive Cameron O'Reilly told reporters.
The group earlier reported calendar 1996 net profit edged up to A$26.54 million from A$26.39 million in 1995.
The group's broadcasting interests were on track to meet current year budgets and were poised for growth in 1997, he said.
O'Reilly said the group's regional newspapers were currently in profit while the magazines division was on target for a good first quarter performance.
In outdoor advertising, further opportunities for growth were being sought, he said.
"We have had a lot of expansion already but there is still plenty of organic growth. We are seeking further opportunities for (outdoor advertising) development," he said.
O'Reilly repeated earlier statement that APN was always an interested observer of developments at the John Fairfax Holdings Ltd newspaper group.
"We are always an interested observer of Fairfax. The situation is very fluid and my guess is it will be resolved in 1997," O'Reilly said.
He said he could only speak on behalf of APN but not for the group's parent company, the Ireland-based Independent Newspapers Plc.
APN is about 49 percent owned by the family interests of Irish businessman Tony O'Reilly and Independent Newspapers, his main media group.
